title: Simulating quantum measurements without superposition devices
summary: Superposition is the core feature that sets quantum theory apart from classical physics. Here, we investigate whether sets of quantum measurements can be modelled by using devices limited to performing jointly diagonalisable measurements. This leads us to introduce classical measurement models, where many such devices are connected together through classical randomness and post-processing. Such classical measurement models are intermediate between the notion of commutative measurements and joint measurability.
